Rashi on Sotah 11b:10:1.english: They recognized Him - For they had already seen His Divine Presence.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:10:2.english: This is my God - That I have already seen.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:11:1.english: Elisheva - the daughter of Amminadav, the wife of Aaron.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:13:1.hebrew: שהיתה פועה לולד - משעשעת אותו, כדרך שמשחקים לתינוקות בדברים ערבים לשעשעו:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:13:1.english: That she would coo to the newborn - She would amuse it, in the way that one plays with infants, with pleasant things to delight it.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:13:2.hebrew: פועה - צועקת, כמו "כיולדה אפעה" (ישעיהו מב):
Rashi on Sotah 11b:13:2.english: Pu'ah - She cries out, like "as a woman in labor I will cry out" (Isaiah 42).

Rashi on Sotah 11b:14:1.hebrew: ה"ג: וראיתן על האבנים. אמר רבי יוחנן: סימן גדול מסר להן, בשעה שכורעת לילד, יריכותיה מצטננות כאבנים. ד"א: על האבנים, כדכתיב וארד בית היוצר וגו' — מה יוצר זה, ירך מכאן כו':
Rashi on Sotah 11b:14:1.english: Some texts read: **"And you shall see them upon the stones."** Rabbi Yochanan said: He gave them a great sign — at the time when she crouches to give birth, her thighs grow cold like stones. Another explanation: "Upon the stones," as it is written, "And I went down to the potter's house," etc. — just as this potter [has a wheel with two stones, one on each side], so too [the woman has a thigh] on this side [and on that side], etc.:

Rashi on Sotah 11b:14:2.hebrew: סימן גדול - שלא תטלנו האם ותחביאנו ותאמר: נפל היה. זה לכם הסימן של לידה, ואז תטלוהו ותהרגוהו. ד"א, להכי קרי ליה למשבר של אשה אבנים, כדכתיב גבי יוצר כלי חרס "אבנים", ואשה נמי ליוצר דמיא:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:14:2.english: A great sign - So that the mother would not take it and hide it and say, "It was a stillbirth." This is the sign of birth for you, and then you may take it and kill it. Another explanation: The reason it calls a woman's birthstool "stones" is because it is written regarding the potter of earthenware vessels "stones" [the potter's wheel], and a woman too is likened to a potter.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:15:1.hebrew: סדן - עץ עב שעליו יושב ומגלגל הבצים, לעשותן בדפוס הכלי לפי גדלו וקטנו:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:15:1.english: Anvil - A thick piece of wood on which [the potter] sits and rolls the lumps [of clay], to shape them in the mold of the vessel according to its largeness or smallness.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:16:1.hebrew: סימן גדול מסר להם - וראיתן על האבנים, אם בן הוא — שם אתן יכולות לראות מיד אם בן הוא, בלא שום הגבהה:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:16:1.english: He gave them a great sign - "And you see them upon the stones" — if it is a boy, there you can see immediately that it is a boy, without any lifting [of the infant].

Rashi on Sotah 11b:16:2.english: A son, [born] with his face downward - In the manner of [his] marital relations.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:16:3.hebrew: בת פניה למעלה - כדרך תשמישתה. והכי מפרש במסכת נדה (דף לא.):
Rashi on Sotah 11b:16:3.english: A daughter whose face is upward - In the normal manner of her marital relations. And so it is explained in tractate Niddah (31a).

Rashi on Sotah 11b:17:1.hebrew: אליהן - משמע על עיסקי ביאה, לשון "ויבא אליה" (בראשית כט):
Rashi on Sotah 11b:17:1.english: To them - This implies [that it was] regarding matters of intercourse, [similar to] the expression "and he came to her" (Genesis 29).

Rashi on Sotah 11b:18:1.hebrew: ותחיין - הוה ליה למיכתב: "ולא המיתו הילדים". "ותחיין" משמע שהיו מסייעין להחיותן, שהיו טומנות אותן בבתיהן ומגדלות אותם:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:18:1.english: And they kept alive - It should have written, "and they did not kill the children." [The word] "and they kept alive" implies that they helped to keep them alive, for they would hide them in their houses and raise them.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:19:1.english: If we say [that "chayot" means] actual animals - [even they have] midwives.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:1:1.hebrew: בפרך - בפה רך. משכום בדברים ובשכר, עד שהרגילום לעבודה:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:1:1.english: With *perekh* - [Read as] *be-feh rakh* (with a soft mouth). They enticed them with words and with payment, until they had accustomed them to the labor.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:1:2.english: With crushing labor - With the breaking of the body and the loins, and with harshness.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:20:1.hebrew: כחיה נמשלה - וחית השדה אינה צריכה למילדת:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:20:1.english: Likened to a wild beast - And a beast of the field does not need a midwife.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:21:1.hebrew: דכתיב ביה כתיב ביה - מי שכתוב בו שנקרא בשם בהמה וחיה, הרי כתיב בו. ושאין כתיב בו, הרי כתיב בכל כנסייתן יחד: מה אמך לביא בין אריות רבצה — אמך, כנסת ישראל כולה, נקראת לביאה:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:21:1.english: Whoever is written about, it is written about him - For one concerning whom it is written that he is called by the name of an animal or beast, behold, it is written about him. And for those concerning whom it is not written, behold, it is written about all their assembly together: "What was your mother? A lioness; among lions she crouched" — "your mother" is the whole congregation of Israel, which is called a lioness.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:22:1.english: Aaron and Moses - Who descended from Yocheved.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:22:2.hebrew: ותמת עזובה אשת כלב - והיא מרים. ולקמן מפרש למה נקראת שמה עזובה, והאי "ותמת" — שנצטרעה:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:22:2.english: And Azuvah, the wife of Caleb, died - She is Miriam. And below [the Gemara] explains why her name was called Azuvah. And this "and she died" [means] that she was afflicted with leprosy.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:22:3.hebrew: ויקח לו כלב את אפרת - לאחר שנתרפאת חזר ולקחה לו. אלמא, אפרת קרי מרים, וכתיב בדוד: "בן איש אפרתי":
Rashi on Sotah 11b:22:3.english: And Caleb took for himself Ephrath - After she was healed [of her leprosy], he went back and took her for himself. Evidently, Ephrath is what Miriam is called, and it is written regarding David, "the son of an Ephrathite man."

Rashi on Sotah 11b:23:1.hebrew: וכלב בן חצרון - פסוק הוא בדברי הימים:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:23:1.english: And Caleb son of Hezron - It is a verse in Chronicles.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:23:2.hebrew: בן יפונה - בן שנפנה מעצת מרגלים. תירוצא הוא דקא מתרץ: לעולם בן חצרון הוא, ולמה נקרא בן יפונה? על שם מעשיו:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:23:2.english: Son of Yefuneh - [This means] the one who turned away from the counsel of the spies. This is a resolution that [the Gemara] is providing: In truth, he is the son of Chetzron, and why is he called "son of Yefuneh"? Because of his deeds.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:24:1.english: The reading is: "And still, he is the son of Kenaz."

Rashi on Sotah 11b:24:2.hebrew: חורגו דקנז - בן אשתו של קנז היה כלב, ונמצא עתניאל אחיו מאמו:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:24:2.english: The stepson of Kenaz - Caleb was the son of Kenaz's wife [from a previous marriage], and it turns out that Othniel was his brother on his mother's side.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:3:1.hebrew: ה"ג בעבודה קשה, אמר רבי שמואל בר נחמני אמר ר' יונתן: שהיו מחליפין וכו' - וזו היא קשה, שלא היו רגילים בכך:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:3:1.english: This is the correct reading: "With hard labor." Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan: That they would switch [the tasks of men and women], etc. - And this is what [made it] hard, that they were not accustomed to it.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:3:2.hebrew: ולמאן דאמר - "בפרך" קמא "בפה רך", האי "בפרך" בתרא ודאי פריכה היא, דהכתיב "וימררו":
Rashi on Sotah 11b:3:2.english: And according to the one who says - that the first "befarech" means "with a soft mouth" [i.e., with gentle speech], this latter "befarech" is certainly [actual] crushing labor, for it is written, "And they embittered [their lives]".

Rashi on Sotah 11b:4:1.hebrew: ושופתות - כשמושיבין הסיר על גבי כירה, קרי לה שפיתה:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:4:1.english: And they set [pots] on the fire - When one sets the pot on top of a stove, it is called "*shefita*."

Rashi on Sotah 11b:4:2.hebrew: אחת של חמין - לרחוץ רגלי בעליהן בשדה:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:4:2.english: One of hot [water] - To wash their husbands' feet in the field.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:5:1.hebrew: בין שפתים - בין מצרי השדות, מקומות צנועין. מצר גבול השדה גבוה מכאן, וחבירו מכאן, וחריץ באמצע:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:5:1.english: Between the borders - Between the boundaries of the fields, [which are] modest places. The boundary of the field is raised on this side, and its neighbor's [boundary is raised] on that side, with a furrow in the middle.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:5:2.hebrew: יונה - ישראל, שנאמר: יונתי תמתי (שיר ו):
Rashi on Sotah 11b:5:2.english: Dove - [This refers to] Israel, as it is stated: "My dove, my perfect one" (Song of Songs 6).

Rashi on Sotah 11b:6:1.english: I roused you - to come out of your mother's womb.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:6:2.english: Your travail - An expression of the pangs of a woman in childbirth (Hosea 13):

Rashi on Sotah 11b:7:2.hebrew: משפר - כמו שעושין לתינוקות ליישב את איבריהם ולתקנן, שניתקין מצער הלידה (ברש"י שבעין יעקב מופיע כאן הלעז: אינמיילולי"ר, שפירושו: לחתל):
Rashi on Sotah 11b:7:2.english: Meshaper - [This means smoothing,] like what is done to infants, to settle their limbs and set them right, for they are dislocated from the pain of birth. (In the Rashi in Ein Yaakov, the Old French gloss appears here: inmeilolir, which means: to swaddle.)

Rashi on Sotah 11b:7:3.hebrew: לא כרת שרך - לא היה לך מיילדת לחתוך טיבור הולד:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:7:3.english: Your umbilical cord was not cut - You had no midwife to cut the newborn's navel cord.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:7:4.hebrew: למשעי - להחליק בשר, כמו חלקת צואריו (בראשית כ״ז:ט״ז), שעיעות:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:7:4.english: Lemish'i - To smooth the flesh, like "the smoothness of his neck" (Genesis 27:16), "se'i'ut" [smoothing].

Rashi on Sotah 11b:7:5.hebrew: עגולין - כעין ככר עגול. נעשה להן נס:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:7:5.english: Round - Like a round loaf. A miracle was performed for them.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:8:1.hebrew: רבבה כצמח השדה - גדילים מן הארץ כצמח השדה:
Rashi on Sotah 11b:8:1.english: Myriads, like the growth of the field - They grew from the ground like the growth of the field.

Rashi on Sotah 11b:9:1.english: And you came - To your father's house.

Tosafot on Sotah 11b:13:1.hebrew: שהיתה פועה לולד - פירש רבינו חננאל: לוחשת לחישה, ויוצא הולד, כמו שעושים אלו עכשיו באזני האמה:
Tosafot on Sotah 11b:13:1.english: That she would "cry out" (po'ah) to the newborn - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: She would whisper a whisper, and the newborn would emerge, like what these [people] do nowadays in the ears of the maidservant.
